Optogenetic distance instead uses a postmortem ChRmine-expression mask, not simultaneous firing measurements. Histological arterial masks are manually registered and refined, not generated causal geometry.

Motion, pupil and locomotion corrections and signal-selection rules affect the analyzed response. In two-photon processing, selected low-power traces are set to zero by an analysis rule. Linear mixed models account for nesting in functional comparisons; the separate resting-diameter test treats vessels as independent despite nesting within mice.

Optogenetic stimulation uses two-second ChRmine pulse trains and six mice per genotype. The zero-laser condition can retain spontaneous vasomotion and imaging-light opsin activation; it is not an opsin-negative control. Functional imaging days 14-16 after viral injection do not specify a universal post-tamoxifen interval.

Propagation velocity is derived from the inverse slope of optical-response onset time versus position along a selected artery, with onset at ten percent of a sigmoid fit. Figure 5E calls it the slope, whereas Methods specify the inverse. Velocity analysis reports thirty averaged repeats, while the general optogenetic protocol reports ninety per power across sessions; subset selection requires clarification.

Full-screen noise differs from focal circles in spatial coverage and pattern. The comparison does not isolate energetic demand, and oxygen consumption or ATP supply is not measured. Time-to-peak genotype differences depend on distance bin; the farthest optogenetic and full-field bins are nonsignificant, not evidence of equivalence.

Resting microvascular control measures capillary RBC velocity near 100 micrometers depth, not whole-brain perfusion or RBC flux. Tail-cuff systolic/diastolic pressure is a separate systemic control. Nonsignificance in these small cohorts does not demonstrate physiological equivalence.

PMC author-manuscript passages and the author-hosted in-press PDF were read, including main Figures 1-6 and supplementary Figures S5-S7. Selected Methods cover the admitted assays; general cloning/culture methods and remaining supplemental material were not fully audited. Final bibliographic pagination is 5003-5019.e22, whereas the read in-press PDF ends its Methods at e12; version completeness remains unresolved.

Separate statistical/genotyping Tables S1-S2, allele-map files and movies were not obtained or replayed. Raw measurements are available from the authors on request and have not been obtained. The paper identifies code DOI 10.7910/DVN/XRRGRI, but public repository access failed; code files were not inspected or executed. No numerical edge weights or independent experimental reproduction are claimed.

Aortic electrical measurements, retinal tracer spread and awake cortical responses are distinct preparations. Cerebral endothelial voltage is not recorded along the full route. Gap junctions can carry small molecules as well as current; residual vascular responses and alternative routes prevent identification of a unique complete neural-to-vascular mechanism.

studies.finding: Partial astrocyte ablation reduced passivity; activation suppressed swimming. NE-MO activation increased astrocyte calcium and suppressed swimming in intact fish. Probabilistic feedback altered calcium accumulation.
limitations: Larval zebrafish, 5-7 days post fertilization; sex undetermined. The fictive-swimming assay uses paralyzed, restrained animals and tail motor-nerve signals, not displacement.

About half the fish did not show open-loop passivity and were excluded from subsequent analyses. Passivity is operationally an inter-swim interval of at least five seconds, not a report of hopelessness or human cognition.

Ablation is partial and may have indirect effects. gfap-driven tools may retain low neuronal expression; activation may affect other ions and second messengers. Convergent controls constrain but do not eliminate these caveats.

The glia-to-neuron molecular mechanism and unique evidence-accumulation algorithm remain unresolved. No universal glial class, minimal cell count, perfect intervention or independently reproduced experiment is asserted.
